bull.b: Broader approval and less frequent dosing can reduce treatment burden and improve adoption in Fabry disease. Continued partner-led commercialization also expands reach without requiring Protalix to build a large direct sales infrastructure.

The shift to positive earnings, strong margins and positive free cash flow indicates that commercial operations can fund a meaningful portion of development. This improves resilience and reduces dependence on external financing.

High liquidity and no debt or warrants give Protalix flexibility to support manufacturing, regulatory work and pipeline development. The absence of scheduled debt obligations also lowers refinancing risk while products and candidates mature.

bear.b: Reliance on Chiesi and variable ordering can make reported revenue difficult to forecast, even when underlying demand is healthy. Concentration also leaves Protalix exposed to a partner's inventory decisions and commercial execution.

The milestone is not a recurring sales stream, and the R&D benefit may not fully offset future cost increases. Consequently, current earnings and margins may overstate the sustainable profitability of the underlying business.

A high antibody rate and unresolved dosing trade-offs could limit efficacy, tolerability or dosing convenience for PRX-115. These issues may delay development, increase trial complexity and reduce the pipeline's eventual commercial value.
